haiku-low.q1: When enqueue_notification writes the monolith row inside the caller's transaction. It exists only if that transaction commits.
haiku-low.q2: The broker is at-least-once, so it redelivers the unacknowledged message after 30 s, possibly to another consumer instance.
haiku-low.q3: 5 tries total, retried 1, 2, 4, then 8 minutes after failure. On the 5th failure the row is failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update first, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, each at least 3 days apart. Before password_reset, order_confirmed needs 3 days on the service and p99 under 60 s.
haiku-low.q5: idempotency_key=notification_id, the UUID made by enqueue_notification. MailRelay remembers keys for 24 h, drops the repeat and returns success.
haiku-low.q6: The monolith's relay publishes service-routed pending rows to notifications.requested every 1 s. The monolith is done once the broker confirms and the row is marked published.
haiku-low.q7: The route column, set once at enqueue from flag notify.route.<type>, read in the caller's transaction. A failed flag read gives monolith.
haiku-low.q8: The ledger insert uses ON CONFLICT (notification_id) DO NOTHING on the primary key, so the duplicate does nothing and is acked.
haiku-low.q9: It acks after committing the ledger insert and before sending. A crash before commit gets redelivered; a crash between commit and ack is redelivered, inserted as nothing, and acked.
haiku-low.q10: In notif-svc's deliveries ledger table. The notif-svc sender polls every 1 s and acts on pending rows with next_attempt_at due.
haiku-low.q11: Nothing changes for them. Rows keep route service and still go through the relay and notif-svc, so nothing is lost or sent twice.
haiku-low.q12: notification_id, type, email, payload and created_at. Email content is rendered inside notif-svc, since templates live in the service now.

sonnet.q1: When the business code's transaction commits, the monolith notifications row (written by enqueue_notification inside that transaction) is the first durable record. If that transaction doesn't commit, the notification doesn't exist.
sonnet.q2: The broker is at-least-once: anything not acked within 30 s is redelivered, possibly to another consumer instance.
sonnet.q3: 5 tries total. After each failure, retry after 1, 2, 4 or 8 minutes (attempts+1, next_attempt_at set). On the 5th failure the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: One type at a time: shipping_update first, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, each at least 3 days on the new service before the next. Before password_reset moves: order_confirmed has had 3 days on notif-svc AND its p99 latency is under 60 s; otherwise fix latency and don't flip. (Also the daily checks passing; password_reset is alerted at p99 60 s and rolled back if breached.)
sonnet.q5: idempotency_key=notification_id (the UUID made by enqueue_notification, the monolith row.id). MailRelay drops the repeat (remembers keys for 24 h) and returns success.
sonnet.q6: Via the outbox relay/publisher in the monolith: it polls every 1 s for route='service', status='pending' rows, publishes each to the broker topic notifications.requested, waits for broker confirmation, sets status published and commits. After published, the monolith is done; it never sends email or retries sends.
sonnet.q7: enqueue_notification decides, at enqueue time, by reading the flag notify.route.<type> within the caller's transaction and writing it to the row's route column (monolith or service). It is set once and never changed (flag takes up to 10 s to propagate).
sonnet.q8: The listener's INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (notification_id) DO NOTHING on the deliveries ledger (notification_id is primary key), so the repeat inserts nothing and is just acked; also MailRelay idempotency key.
sonnet.q9: It acks after the commit of the ledger insert and before anything is sent. Crash before commit: message redelivered after 30 s. Crash between commit and ack: redelivery's insert does nothing and it is just acked.
sonnet.q10: In the notif-svc ledger (deliveries table in its own database): status, attempts, next_attempt_at. The notif-svc sender acts on it, polling every 1 s for up to 50 pending rows with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
sonnet.q11: Nothing changes for them. Rolling back is the flag going back to monolith; rows already routed to service keep route service, still go through the outbox publisher and are sent by notif-svc (publisher and service keep running). Only new rows go to the old worker. Nothing lost or sent twice.
sonnet.q12: The message carries notification_id, type, email, payload, created_at. The email content is rendered in notif-svc (templates live in the service), at send time.
